metaData.originalTitle: PRD → Goal → After-Goal：AI 主导全流程研发实践
metaData.title: PRD → Goal → After-Goal: AI-Led Full-Process Development Practice
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article demonstrates, through a real-world case, how to use Claude Code's three slash commands — /prd, /goal, and /after-goal — to achieve a fully automated development workflow from requirement breakdown to code merge.
metaData.summary: The article details the author's experience in Baidu's internal R&D environment, leveraging Claude Code's Skill mechanism and three slash commands to fully automate the development of a product feature called "self-evolution." The workflow is divided into three phases: the /prd phase transforms vague requirements into a structured PRD document and automatically splits them into iCafe cards; the /goal phase implements code for each card and automatically writes tests; the /after-goal phase automatically completes code commits, Gerrit pushes, scoring and merging, card updates, and closure. The article summarizes best practices such as prioritizing PRD, controlling card granularity, preferring CLI over browsers, and using Skills as carriers of process knowledge. It also compares this approach with the Autoresearch solution, offering a lightweight, fully automated, and reusable solution for AI-assisted development.

mainPoints.point: PRD first is a prerequisite for efficient AI development, preventing requirement deviations and rework.
mainPoints.explanation: Directly asking AI to write code often leads to deviations from requirements. Using /prd to first generate a structured PRD document — clarifying user stories, acceptance criteria, and non-goals — and then breaking it down into appropriately sized cards enables AI to implement efficiently and accurately.

mainPoints.point: Card granularity must be appropriate, and dependency order determines the implementation sequence.
mainPoints.explanation: The cards broken down this time were independent with clear acceptance criteria, allowing AI to implement them correctly in one go. Implementing in dependency order avoids conflicts from modifying multiple packages simultaneously and ensures each card can be independently verified upon completion.

mainPoints.point: CLI tools are superior to browser operations, and Skills are effective carriers of process knowledge.
mainPoints.explanation: Any operation achievable via CLI should not be done through a browser, as this greatly improves efficiency. Solidifying the complete workflow of "commit → push → score → merge → update → close" into a Skill enables automated process closure and knowledge accumulation.

mainPoints.point: The three-phase collaboration model achieves full-process automation from requirements to deployment.
mainPoints.explanation: /prd involves humans directing the direction with AI assisting in breakdown; /goal involves AI leading implementation with humans verifying results; /after-goal involves AI fully automating the process closure. This forms a reusable, lightweight, fully automated development workflow.

keyQuotes: Directly asking AI to write code often leads to misunderstandings of requirements and missed edge cases. PRD forces you to think things through first.
Any operation achievable via CLI should not be done through a browser.
The process of writing a Skill is itself a process of organizing workflows and accumulating knowledge.
Fix issues as soon as you encounter them; don't leave them for later. The cost of early fixes is the lowest.

The three phases each have their focus: /prd involves humans directing the direction with AI assisting in breakdown, /goal involves AI leading implementation with humans verifying results, and /after-goal involves AI fully automating the process closure.
